report.summary: Chunk 3 of 4 of mutate.py: implements mutation operators (DROP_CALL, INVERT_CONDITION, WEAKEN_COMPARISON, CHANGE_CONSTANT, DROP_ARGUMENT, EARLY_RETURN) and the generate function skeleton with filtering logic.
risks: EARLY_RETURN insertion after docstring | medium | The comment claims that inserting after docstring is critical to avoid a measurement artefact; the code implements this by skipping docstring expressions. If the docstring is not at body[0] (e.g., a comment-only function), the logic might still work but the comment's reasoning may not hold. Inspection of the actual measurement would settle it.

filtered dict never used | high | The variable `filtered` is defined and populated via `_refuse` but never read or returned; it is dead code. This was noted in the comment as a defect. Adding logging or returning it would settle it.

SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, _in_main_block, covered_lines are referenced but not defined in this chunk | high | These symbols are used in conditions but their definitions are outside this chunk; if missing, the code will raise NameError. Their definitions in the same file would settle it.

DROP_ARGUMENT check len(target.args) < 1 after already checking node.args | low | The condition `if len(target.args) < 1` is redundant because the site collection already requires `node.args` non-empty. Could be simplified.

WEAKEN_COMPARISON swap dictionary missing ast.Is, ast.IsNot, ast.In, ast.NotIn | low | The operator only handles Lt, Gt, LtE, GtE, Eq, NotEq. Other comparison operators are ignored, which is intentional but may be unexpected.

CHANGE_CONSTANT increments string by appending '_x' | low | For string constants, appending '_x' changes the value; this is a valid mutation but the comment does not specify the exact transformation. Could be considered a design choice.

generate function signature uses `include` parameter default 'daedalus' | low | The default path may not exist in all repos; if missing, `files` will be empty and generation returns []. This is documented in the comment 'if not files: return []'.
max_files default 400 may truncate corpus | low | The comment says 'Deterministic' but the truncation to 400 files is not mentioned. If the repo has more files, some are silently ignored.
todos: Verify that SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, _in_main_block, covered_lines are defined elsewhere in the file.
Consider using or removing the `filtered` dict to avoid dead code.
Add test for the EARLY_RETURN docstring-skipping logic to ensure it works for functions without docstrings.

claims.text: AFTER the docstring, never before. Inserting ahead of it demotes the docstring from body[0] to an ordinary string expression, which makes a LITERAL appear out of nowhere -- an artefact of the generator that was measured suppressing detection of this operator from ~100% to 37%.
claims.why: The code implements this: it skips a docstring expression at body[0] (lines 243-245) and inserts the Return after the docstring (lines 250-251). The claim about measurement is uncheckable but the implementation matches the described behaviour.

claims.text: MEASURED 2026-07-30: these filters were defined, documented as built, and CALLED FROM NOWHERE. Every one of SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, _in_main_block and covered_lines appeared exactly once in this file -- its own definition. The corpus behind the published 75.3% detection figure was therefore minted without any of them, including on __repr__ bodies and log strings, which is precisely what they exist to exclude.
claims.why: The comment refers to symbols that are used in the code (SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS) but not defined in this chunk. The claim that they appear only once in the file cannot be verified without the full file. The claim about the corpus and detection figure is also outside this chunk.

claims.text: Collect candidate (file, function) sites once, then sample from them, so a big file cannot dominate merely by being walked first.
claims.why: The code collects all sites into a list before sampling (lines 252-253), preventing order bias. The implementation matches the claim.

claims.text: Why each site was refused. Reported rather than discarded, because a filter nobody can see the effect of is the same shape of defect as a filter nobody calls -- see below.
claims.why: The `filtered` dict is populated via `_refuse` but never used (read or returned). It is effectively discarded. The comment says it is reported, but the code does not report it anywhere in this chunk.

claims.text: Generate ``count`` parseable mutants over real functions. Deterministic.
claims.why: The function uses a fixed seed for random and returns mutants that are parseable (since they are generated from valid ASTs). The determinism is ensured by the seed.

observations.what: The `filtered` dict is defined and populated but never used; it is dead code.
References to SKIP_PATH_PARTS, SKIP_FUNCTIONS, _is_display_constant, _looks_like_a_guard, _in_main_block, covered_lines are used but not defined in this chunk.
The EARLY_RETURN operator skips a docstring expression at body[0] before inserting a Return. The comment claims this avoids a measurement artefact.
The generate function collects all sites before sampling, preventing order bias.
The WEAKEN_COMPARISON operator swaps comparison operators using a dictionary that only covers Lt, Gt, LtE, GtE, Eq, NotEq.
